zh.title: 聯合航空拓展國際航線 新增沖繩為日本第六個航點
zh.summary: 聯合航空新增沖繩航點；以波音777每週營運三班；成為唯一直飛琉球之北美航空
body: 美國聯合航空（United Airlines）宣布新增日本沖繩為其第六個日本航點，此項舉措屬於該航空公司大規模國際拓展計畫的一環。聯合航空預計使用波音777客機，提供每週三班的直飛服務，直接連結琉球群島。
根據 Simple Flying 報導，開通此航點後，聯合航空成為目前唯一提供直飛服務連結琉球群島的北美航空公司。該項每週三班的營運計畫，將進一步豐富其在日本市場的航線佈局與國際航網。
聯合航空透過引進每週三班的波音777長程廣體客機服務，持續擴大其在日本與國際市場的業務涵蓋範圍，並使沖繩成為其在該國開闢的第六個營運據點。

en.title: United Adds Okinawa As 6th Japanese Destination With Thrice-Weekly 777 Flights
en.summary: United adds Okinawa as its sixth Japanese destination with thrice-weekly Boeing 777 direct flights.
body: United Airlines is adding Okinawa as its sixth destination in Japan as part of its largest international expansion. The carrier plans to operate a thrice-weekly Boeing 777 service to directly link the Ryukyu islands.

With this new route, United becomes the only North American airline to offer direct flights to the Ryukyu islands. The thrice-weekly service expands the carrier's overall Japanese destination network.

According to Simple Flying, the addition of Okinawa strengthens direct connectivity for the carrier in Japan. The Boeing 777 widebody service marks United's sixth Japanese destination in its ongoing international route expansion.

zh.title: 美國撤銷敘利亞支恐指定 解除航班往返禁令
zh.summary: 美國撤銷敘利亞支援恐怖主義國家登記；國務院豁免敘利亞航班往返美國禁令
body: 美國於2026年8月24日將敘利亞從支援恐怖主義國家名單中除名，並進一步推動解除對敘利亞擁有或控制之航班往返美國的限制。美國國務卿盧比歐（Marco Rubio）在完成45天的國會審查程序後正式撤銷該項指定，標誌著美國對敘利亞航空業相關法律限制的重大調整。
美國國務院同時豁免了依據《化學與生物武器管制與消除戰爭法案》實施的剩餘限制措施，其中包括禁止由敘利亞擁有或控制的航空運輸事業往返美國。國會已於8月24日收到相關豁免通知。根據美國財政部發布的更新指引，該豁免措施將於通知送達20天後正式生效。
美國官方強調，該項豁免並不代表敘利亞籍航空公司可立即獲准開航美國航線。任何有意進入美國市場的航空公司，仍須取得相關的經濟、飛安、航空安保與營運審查批准。此外，美方對部分特定個人與組織的針對性制裁依然有效，航空製造商與相關機構仍須遵守相關合規規範。
在出口管制方面，美國商務部此前已調整針對敘利亞的出口限制，並擴大了針對替換零件、飛機零組件及特定臨時飛機營運的許可豁免。美國商務部指出，針對支援民用航空領域的出口許可申請，只要相關項目不會對敘利亞的軍事能力或支援國際恐怖主義的能力產生重大貢獻，將採取預設批准原則進行審查。
敘利亞近期已著手恢復部分因長期衝突而中斷的國際航線。根據報導，敘利亞航空（Syrian Airlines）已恢復大馬士革往返莫斯科、阿姆斯特丹與麥地那的航班服務；同時，德國航空公司 Sundair 與 LEAV Aviation 也已規劃或啟動往返大馬士革及代爾祖爾等地的航班營運。

en.title: US Rescinds Syria Terror Designation and Moves to Lift Aviation Restrictions
en.summary: US State Department rescinds Syria terrorism status, waiving ban on Syrian flight operations.
body: The United States has removed Syria from its official list of state sponsors of terrorism and initiated measures to remove longstanding legal restrictions on Syrian-owned or controlled flights operating to and from the US. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio formally rescinded the terrorism designation on August 24, 2026, following the completion of a required 45-day congressional review period.

As part of these regulatory adjustments, the US State Department also waived remaining statutory restrictions imposed under the Chemical and Biological Weapons Control and Warfare Elimination Act. These included a prohibition against Syrian-owned or controlled air transportation serving US destinations. The United States Congress was formally notified of the waiver on August 24, and updated Treasury Department guidance specifies that the measure will take effect 20 days after notification.

US authorities emphasized that this statutory waiver does not confer immediate regulatory approval for any Syrian airline to launch direct flights to the United States. Any air carrier seeking to serve the American market must still obtain all applicable economic, flight safety, aviation security, and operational approvals. Furthermore, targeted sanctions against specific individuals and designated organizations remain in place, requiring aviation sector firms to maintain compliance protocols.

On the trade front, the US Commerce Department previously eased broader export restrictions and expanded regulatory license exceptions covering aircraft components, replacement parts, and temporary aircraft operations. The department noted that applications supporting civil commercial aviation are reviewed under a presumption of approval, provided that the requested equipment or technology does not make a significant contribution to military capabilities or international terrorism.

Amid these regulatory developments, international flight services to Syria have progressively resumed across several routes. State carrier Syrian Airlines has restored air connections linking Damascus with Moscow, Amsterdam, and Madinah. Concurrently, European carriers including Sundair and LEAV Aviation have commenced or announced scheduled passenger operations connecting German cities with Syrian airports in Damascus and Deir Ezzor.
